question.text: Fund Artha Hedge LLP receives SEBI in-principle approval for a Category III AIF. Which activity is permissible BEFORE obtaining the Registration Certificate in Form B?

answer.text: Declaring First Close and calling money from investors
Approaching investors to raise capital commitments but NOT collecting money
Listing units on a recognised stock exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Step 4, after in-principle approval the AIF may appoint distributors and take capital commitments from investors, but cannot collect money until the Registration Certificate (Form B) is issued. The Trap: First Close, NAV declaration, and listing are all later steps (Steps 6, 6, and post-final-close respectively). Cross-Exam Context: Identical sequencing applies to Cat I/II AIFs under XIX-A — commitment ≠ call. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Commit letters can be executed at Step 4, but bank/custody/demat accounts should be opened in parallel to avoid delay at First Close.
